headline: Earnings sink on costs and volume; guidance holds
summary_short: Net sales fell 3.3% to $3.10B on lower volumes and cost inflation, and GAAP income before taxes dropped 49.0% to $283.1M; the company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance.
summary_long: Net sales declined 3.3% (3.6% constant currency) to $3.10B as a 5.4% drop in financial volume outweighed favorable pricing and mix. COGS per hectoliter rose 12.1%, driven by a $98.0M unfavorable mark-to-market swing on commodity derivatives, elevated Midwest Premium-related costs (~$40M), and volume deleverage, partially offset by cost-savings initiatives. GAAP income before taxes fell 49.0% to $283.1M; diluted EPS fell 42.3% to $1.23. Cash rose to $2.13B after $1.85B of new debt issuance used to refinance upcoming note maturities. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance across net sales, underlying EPS, capex, and free cash flow targets.

drivers.explanation: Net sales fell on a 5.4% financial-volume decline in the Americas and EMEA&APAC, partly offset by favorable pricing/mix and FX.
COGS per hectoliter rose 12.1%, driven by a $98.0M unrealized mark-to-market swing on commodity derivatives and Midwest Premium-related cost inflation.
Higher COGS and a 3.7% rise in MG&A, from cycling lower prior-year incentive comp and ERP implementation costs, outweighed pricing gains and cost savings.
Same COGS/MG&A pressure plus lower other non-operating income from an approximately $18M unfavorable Fever-Tree investment fair-value swing.
Tracks the pre-tax income decline, partially cushioned by a lower effective tax rate (22% vs 24%) from a higher discrete tax benefit.
Falls less than net income in percentage terms because weighted-average diluted shares fell to 187.7M from 201.2M on share repurchases.
Cash builds after $1.85B of new senior notes issued in May 2026, held to repay $2.0B of notes maturing shortly after quarter-end.
Management cites heightened macro headwinds pressuring consumer behavior and input costs, with disciplined execution and cost-savings initiatives cited as mitigants.
